objective: Proof. On every Fano tree, show that every ordered pair of lines of a Fano atom gets one and the same native far-side vector, by composing the atom with the deep relations its closed sides can present (floor: a leaf behind every cut; ceiling: the largest state Fano-tree sides reach), checked against exact maps. Derive that FAR-READ B's split step cuts atoms once vectors are native, and that on Fano trees the native reading is the yes/no twin rule.
status: Proved: in every Fano tree every ordered pair of lines of a Fano atom gets one native vector (253 configurations, 2,990 pairs, floor = ceiling over all states closed sides can show; composition exact on 12 built trees), atoms act as one natively (ATOM-ONE B's bound at every gluing order), so FAR-READ B's split step cuts atoms natively (0 of 23 Fano trees read; 23 of 23 in the stored order) and the native reading of Fano trees is the yes/no twin rule
title: Natively a Fano atom is homogeneous
